name: Make
summary: Make (formerly Integromat) lets you build workflows, called scenarios, by dragging app modules onto a visual map, run on Make's servers.

free_plan_covers.note: The Free plan gives 1,000 credits a month and 2 active scenarios, with scheduled runs at most every 15 minutes. Each module action in a run uses a credit, so a 3 step scenario runs about 330 times a month.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The Core plan is $12 a month for 10,000 credits, with unlimited active scenarios and runs as often as every minute. Paying yearly saves 15% or more.

portability.note: Scenarios are built from Make's own app modules and only run on Make, so moving away means rebuilding each one in another tool.

self_hostable.note: Every plan on the pricing page, Enterprise included, runs on Make's own cloud; there is no version to install on your own server.

code_steps.note: The Make Code app runs JavaScript or Python in a scenario and uses 2 credits per second of run time. It is in open beta; its docs say paid plans, while the pricing page lists it on every plan.

webhook_triggers.note: The Custom Webhook module gives a scenario a web address your app can call, and Make starts the run as soon as a request arrives. Make accepts up to 300 webhook requests every 10 seconds.

setup.step: Create a Make account; the Free plan is enough to build and test a scenario.
Start the scenario with a Custom Webhook module, add a webhook, and copy its address into your app's environment file.

builder_notes: Call the Make webhook from server code only, reading the address from MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL.
Make answers a webhook with "Accepted" right away and runs the scenario after, so don't wait on the call for a result unless the scenario ends with a Webhook Response module.
